newsitem.title: UK: UK records first case of BSE in a cow born in 1994.
newsitem.headline: UK records first case of BSE in a cow born in 1994.

text.p: Mad cow disease has been confirmed in a cow born in Wales in January 1994, the first known case in Britain in an animal born in that year, British Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham said on Wednesday.

"This is the first case of BSE in an animal born in 1994 but is unlikely to be the last, as the risk of exposure through feed was not significantly different in the early months of 1994 compared with the closing months of 1993, when cases have already been confirmed," he said in a written parliamentary answer.
Britain banned the use of animal feed incorporating cattle offal, which is thought most likely to harbour the BSE agent, in 1990.

But ministers have acknowledged that the regulations were not enforced as strictly as they might have been until scientists reported evidence in March 1996 that mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), could probably be transmitted to humans.
